baloyi.role: MK, first on its Johannesburg list

dooms.role: Political analyst, director of the Rivonia Circle

items.h: ANC and MK Party seal eThekwini coalition deal as ActionSA’s future hangs in balance
items.s: Teke reported ANC and MK insiders saying a deal had been finalised in eThekwini, with MK set to take the mayoralty, while ActionSA’s part was still being negotiated.

items.h: Coalition talks could shut DA out of eThekwini and Johannesburg
items.s: Teke reported that the talks were heading towards an MK-led coalition with the ANC, EFF and ActionSA in eThekwini, which could keep the DA out there and in Johannesburg.

items.h: Rumoured ActionSA–ANC pact: just add water
items.s: In a satirical column, Butler mocked the rumoured ActionSA–ANC pact for Johannesburg and the leaked draft agreement said to be circulating.

items.h: Parties may strike deniable deals to avoid formal coalitions
items.s: Butler argued that the ANC and DA have treated coalition talks as too important to leave to councillors, and warned that informal, deniable deals and minority governments may only leave councils more fragile.

items.h: Mayor Herman Mashaba loading?
items.s: On SMWX, Nkadimeng looked at Johannesburg’s first council sitting since the election results were declared, as the city chases the 27 November deadline to elect its leadership.

items.h: The DA won the most votes in Tshwane. Cilliers Brink may still not be mayor
items.s: On Conversations with Gabriel, Cilliers Brink told Makin why the DA offered ActionSA the Tshwane mayoralty, why that offer was dismissed, and how the DA’s offer to the ANC on 137 hung councils would work.

items.h: ActionSA’s Michael Beaumont on the coalitions, Mashaba, Zille and Joburg
items.s: On SMWX, Mpofu-Walsh spoke to ActionSA’s Michael Beaumont about the party’s push for Herman Mashaba in Johannesburg and Nasiphi Moya in Tshwane, its red lines on Helen Zille and Cilliers Brink, and the offer he says the DA rejected.

items.h: MK Party’s busy with multi-party coalition negotiations in eThekwini
items.s: Mngambi spoke to MK’s KwaZulu-Natal leader Willies Mchunu, who said the national leadership was leading talks with the ANC, EFF, ActionSA and IFP, and that the DA had approached the party, though he knew of no concrete engagement.

items.h: Business sector weighs in as Friday coalition deadline looms
items.s: Mngambi spoke to Cape Chamber of Commerce and Industry CEO John Lawson about what the coalition talks in hung municipalities mean for business confidence, investment and stable local government.

items.h: Is a Doomsday pact Ramaphosa’s parting shot to SA?
items.s: Written as ANC and MK leaders met in Johannesburg for coalition talks. Helen Zille has conceded, so the DA topped Joburg’s vote but is heading to the opposition benches.

items.h: DA refuses to drop Helen Zille as ActionSA edges closer to an ANC deal
items.s: Geordin Hill-Lewis told Manyathela the DA would not drop Zille as its Joburg candidate and would accept opposition if it came to that. ActionSA chair Michael Beaumont called the ANC’s offer attractive and said the DA had never really held talks with ActionSA.

items.h: Will the GNU survive the coalition bloodbath?
items.s: Basson warns that the national unity government could collapse if the ANC cuts the DA out of city governments.

items.h: Stand by for GNU 2.0, with or without ActionSA
items.s: Basson argues a GNU-style deal led by the DA and ANC is the most likely way the 138 hung councils will be run, and that ActionSA’s Nasiphi Moya could return as Tshwane mayor.

items.h: Mashaba: any coalition deal involving ActionSA must retain Moya as Tshwane mayor
items.s: Speaking to Manyathela at the IEC results centre, Herman Mashaba said ActionSA could set terms with both the DA and the ANC, that Nasiphi Moya must stay on in Tshwane, and that he would not negotiate with a DA team that includes Helen Zille.

items.h: The deal: 4 scenarios for coalitions in our cities and towns
items.s: Basson sets out four coalition line-ups that could decide who governs South Africa’s municipalities, three of them named after national flags with the same colours.

items.h: The 24 hours that rewrote SA’s local politics
items.s: In his Friday Briefing video, Basson notes that the ANC will not control a single one of South Africa’s metros.

items.h: The ANC’s reckoning has come, and it is devastating
items.s: Du Toit writes that the ANC is on the brink of falling to second, third or fourth place in seven of the eight metros.

items.h: Mayor Zille and a DA-ANC Johannesburg coalition? Not too far-fetched
items.s: Du Toit sees a Zille administration working with the ANC’s more moderate wing as possible, though he expects it to be very hard to negotiate.

items.h: The repudiation and diminishing of the ANC
items.s: Before the vote, du Toit argued the municipal election could confirm that the ANC’s decline is speeding up.

items.h: ActionSA snubs DA as ANC weighs coalition deals with MK Party
items.s: Beaumont pushed back at critics, mostly DA supporters, saying ActionSA does not serve at the pleasure of any other party. He said it is set to lead Tshwane again and take over in Johannesburg.

items.h: Michael Beaumont on ActionSA’s coalition hand and the DA standoff
items.s: Beaumont spoke to BizNews’s Alec Hogg about the tensions with the DA, ActionSA’s talks with the ANC and coalition politics.

items.h: On 702: the ANC’s offer is attractive
items.s: Speaking to Clement Manyathela, Beaumont said the ANC’s offer appealed to ActionSA, that the DA had never really held talks with the party, and that any deal still needs a shared programme.

items.h: ActionSA responds to arguments that the DA should lead because it got more votes
items.s: Beaumont said talks with both the DA and ANC are making progress, and that where no party has a majority, coalitions decide who governs. He named the DA’s and ActionSA’s mayoral candidates in Gauteng as the sticking point.

items.h: ActionSA and ANC in coalition discussions
items.s: After meeting the ANC’s Fikile Mbalula and Nomvula Mokonyane, Beaumont called it a productive and respectful first meeting on how to form stable coalition governments, and said ActionSA would talk to all parties the same way.

items.h: On 702: any deal must keep Moya as Tshwane mayor
items.s: Speaking to Clement Manyathela on election night, Mashaba said ActionSA could set terms with both the DA and the ANC, that Nasiphi Moya must stay as Tshwane mayor, and that he would not negotiate with a DA team that includes Helen Zille.

items.h: ANC deals DA out of the Gauteng metros
items.s: Mashaba told the Mail & Guardian that talks with the DA stalled because it would not drop Helen Zille and Cilliers Brink as mayoral candidates. He said ActionSA was drafting a coalition agreement and hoped to sign with the other parties within a day or two.

items.h: Zille concedes defeat in Johannesburg as DA set for opposition benches
items.s: In a message to DA caucus members, Zille conceded that her race for Johannesburg mayor appeared to be over, saying the die seemed to be cast.

items.h: Zille concedes Johannesburg mayoral race as DA coalition talks continue
items.s: Zille told her caucus to prepare for opposition and said she believes an ANC-ActionSA-EFF-MK coalition would be unstable. She said the DA can still help make sure Johannesburg has a working government this term. The DA said this was not its official position and that talks were continuing.

items.h: On 702: the DA will not drop Zille
items.s: Speaking to Clement Manyathela, Hill-Lewis refused to drop Zille as the DA’s Johannesburg candidate, said the DA would keep working until the first council meetings, and said it would accept opposition if needed.

items.h: DA makes offer to ANC, IFP to co-govern 137 hung municipalities
items.s: Hill-Lewis said the DA’s offer, where the party with the most votes in each hung council leads it, would fix local government across the country. He said residents cannot afford another five years of instability.

items.h: ActionSA rejects DA’s coalition offer in hung Gauteng metros
items.s: Beaumont said the DA’s offer was unworkable because ActionSA’s votes would elect two mayors in governments it would not be part of, and that ActionSA would not support a Zille mayoralty.

items.h: Ramaphosa warns parties ahead of coalition talks
items.s: Speaking at the IEC results announcement, Ramaphosa said hung councils are not a failure of democracy. He urged parties to negotiate in good faith rather than fight over positions and power, and warned against delays in forming councils.

items.h: Ramaphosa urges political parties to cooperate on coalition discussions
items.s: In his weekly newsletter, Ramaphosa told parties to cooperate in good faith so councils can be formed and start working, and said councillors must find common ground from the start, whatever their party differences.

items.h: Ramaphosa urges ANC to avoid DA in Johannesburg coalition
items.s: Not said in public. The Sunday Times, citing unnamed insiders, reported that Ramaphosa told a closed ANC meeting to explore a Johannesburg coalition without the DA. ANC spokesperson Mahlengi Bhengu dismissed claims that he had stated a preference.

items.h: I’ve looked at the election, here’s what could happen…
items.s: Mpofu-Walsh goes through the possible coalitions and debuts his idea for one arrangement across South Africa. Commentator Sindile Vabaza describes it as a grand agreement in which the DA, ANC and ActionSA share out the mayors of all eight metros.

items.h: Election update: will the GNU survive?
items.s: Mpofu-Walsh looks at what the local election results mean for the national unity government.

items.h: Could the ANC abandon the DA in coalitions?
items.s: Mpofu-Walsh works through coalition line-ups with and without the DA and the ANC, and what each would mean for the national unity government.

items.h: Coalitions: a major shake-up in SA politics?
items.s: Mpofu-Walsh asks whether South Africa is entering a fundamental political realignment, looking at Mashaba and Moya leading Gauteng metros and an MK-IFP arrangement in KwaZulu-Natal.

items.h: Penuel The Black Pen says he is voting ActionSA for Joburg despite reservations
items.s: Before the vote, Mlotshwa posted on X that he would vote ActionSA in Johannesburg, not because he believed in the party but because he could not see a better one to run the city. He ruled out the ANC, DA, EFF, MK and PA.

items.h: Doubts about ActionSA voters who want a DA deal
items.s: Replying to Clement Manyathela on X, Mlotshwa said he does not trust people who claim to have voted ActionSA but believe the DA is its best coalition partner.

items.h: The DA won’t win the coalition games if it is arrogant
items.s: Mlotshwa posted that the DA won’t win the coalition games if it is arrogant and condescending, and made a video telling DA voters and politicians not to be arrogant in the negotiations.

items.h: Coalition negotiations should be filmed live
items.s: Mlotshwa said coalition negotiations should be filmed live and made public rather than held in secret, and followed it with a video making the same case.

items.h: Here are my 4 coalition scenarios
items.s: Basson named his four coalition scenarios on X: Ukraine, Lesotho, Rainbow and Ghana.

items.h: Play kingmaker: build the coalition you’d back
items.s: Basson shared News24’s Coalition Calculator, inviting readers to try building governments themselves.

items.h: Coalition talks begin
items.s: In a video column, Basson said the real work starts now: fourteen days of coalition negotiations to decide who governs the country’s councils.

items.h: On the brink of Doomsday? Coalition analysis
items.s: Basson shared a video analysis of the coalition talks under the title On the Brink of Doomsday?

items.h: Divergence: DA, ANC now on a collision course ahead of 2029
items.s: Du Toit’s column says the DA and ANC are now on a collision course ahead of the 2029 national election.

items.h: Four possible coalition agreements
items.s: In a video clip, Mpofu-Walsh sets out four coalition scenarios he has in mind, starting with the simplest to understand.

items.h: Across the Desk: the anatomy of coalition politics
items.s: Manyathela’s 702 show unpacked how coalition politics works as the talks began.

items.h: Open Line: DA approaches EFF for coalition talks
items.s: Manyathela and his listeners discussed the DA opening coalition talks with the EFF and MK.

items.h: Coalition talks update
items.s: Manyathela spoke to ActionSA’s Michael Beaumont and the DA’s Geordin Hill-Lewis about how far their talks had got.

items.h: ActionSA and DA coalition talks: latest developments
items.s: Manyathela asked Geordin Hill-Lewis about claims that he and Helen Zille were considering a mayoral swap.

items.h: Open Line: reactions to coalition negotiations
items.s: Listeners reacted on Manyathela’s show to the coalition negotiations and the governments forming in Gauteng.

items.h: We don’t have a problem working with the DA
items.s: Beaumont said ActionSA has no problem working with the DA and is finalising deals with it in some municipalities, but that there are limits to what it will support.

items.h: How Helen Zille broke a working coalition in Johannesburg
items.s: Beaumont posted a video explaining how, in ActionSA’s view, Zille broke a working coalition in Johannesburg, and why the party refuses to give her a second chance.

items.h: Coalition talks are a contest, but they don’t have to be
items.s: In a News24 column, Mashaba wrote that coalition talks are a contest, but argued they do not have to be.

items.h: Coalitions are about choosing the least bad option
items.s: Before the vote, Zille told eNCA that coalition talks are often about choosing the least bad option, and accused smaller parties of putting positions first.

items.h: The DA will publish all its coalition agreements
items.s: Hill-Lewis said the DA will work to build stable governments and will publish all its coalition agreements once they are concluded.

items.h: Hill-Lewis calls mayoral-swap reports dramatic
items.s: Hill-Lewis dismissed as dramatic the reports that he had offered to step down as Cape Town mayor.

items.h: The DA’s final offer to ActionSA
items.s: Hill-Lewis set out the DA’s final offer to ActionSA to govern Gauteng’s three big metros together.

items.h: ‘You wrote off uMkhonto weSizwe’, says Mpofu as party prepares for coalition talks
items.s: Mpofu said MK’s near-10% national vote shows voters want parties to cooperate. He said any deal must rest on shared policy and be concluded within 100 days of a council being set up, with MK’s leadership having the final say, and that at least 120 councils could be hung.

items.h: MK Party warns ANC to reconsider coalition partners
items.s: Mpofu warned that the ANC working with parties whose interests oppose its own could lead to its demise, and said MK did not want the talks to turn into a slanging match.

items.h: MK Party coalition talks, on 702
items.s: Mpofu spoke to Mandy Wiener on 702’s Midday Report about MK’s coalition talks.

items.h: MK’s first meeting with the DA
items.s: Mpofu described MK’s first-ever meeting with the DA as historic and said it had its own significance, but that MK will focus its coalition talks on like-minded parties.

items.h: Mpofu confirms Hill-Lewis asked for coalition talks
items.s: Mpofu confirmed that DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis had asked MK for coalition talks.

items.h: MK’s coalition talks with the ANC, EFF and ActionSA continue
items.s: In a video from MK, Mpofu gave an update on the party’s continuing coalition talks with the ANC, EFF and ActionSA, including in eThekwini.

items.h: Malema tells voters EFF is a ‘stable coalition partner’
items.s: At the EFF’s final rally in Soweto, Malema called the EFF the most stable coalition partner and said coalition government is the future of municipalities. He said the EFF respects coalitions but will not protect wrongdoing, even if it costs the party positions.

items.h: Malema blames the ANC-DA coalition as the EFF reels from losses
items.s: Malema blamed the ANC’s decision to govern nationally with the DA for strengthening white supremacy, saying the local results reflected that deal, and said progressive parties must unite rather than split their support.

items.h: EFF calls on ANC to reconsider DA coalition
items.s: At the IEC results centre, Malema called on the ANC to reconcile with its lost kids, the EFF, MK and SACP, and stand against their common political enemies. EWN reports the EFF wants to join the talks, but on its own terms.

items.h: ANC draws MKP into grand coalition with ActionSA
items.s: News24 reports that the ANC’s negotiating team, led by Mbalula, has drawn MK into a grand coalition with ActionSA, as the ANC’s national executive meets to seal the deal.

items.h: Moya says the results are a vote of confidence
items.s: Moya told eNCA the election numbers are a vote of confidence in her leadership, and credited Tshwane residents for backing her.

items.h: IFP opens coalition talks after winning control of five KZN municipalities
items.s: Hlabisa said the IFP would appoint a negotiating team to lead its coalition talks, after winning outright control of five KwaZulu-Natal municipalities.

items.h: Hlabisa says IFP will seal coalition deals this weekend
items.s: Hlabisa said the IFP expects to seal its municipal coalition agreements this weekend, after meeting the ANC late into the evening.

items.h: McKenzie on the coalition talks, on BizNews
items.s: McKenzie spoke to BizNews’s Alec Hogg on the morning the ANC’s national executive met to decide its coalition path.

items.h: McKenzie pulls the PA out of ANC coalition talks in Upington
items.s: McKenzie has reportedly walked away from coalition talks with the ANC in Dawid Kruiper municipality in the Northern Cape, after a fight over the mayoral post.

items.h: Shivambu rubbishes the ‘left will tank the economy’ scare
items.s: Shivambu dismissed reports that a coalition of left-leaning parties would collapse business confidence and sink the rand, calling the warnings elite propaganda.

items.h: Sarupen: talks with all parties are continuing
items.s: As News24 reported the ANC drawing MK into a deal with ActionSA, Sarupen disputed that the DA had been shut out, saying its talks with all parties were continuing.

items.h: The DA’s full proposal to the ANC
items.s: Sarupen signed the DA’s letter to ANC secretary-general Fikile Mbalula proposing that the two parties, with the IFP, co-govern the hung councils.

items.h: Mulder warns against a DA-ANC deal in Johannesburg
items.s: Mulder warned that a DA-ANC coalition in Johannesburg could end cooperation between the FF Plus and the DA across the country.

items.h: FF Plus fails to broker a DA-ActionSA coalition
items.s: Daily Maverick reports that Mulder held one-on-one talks with the DA and ActionSA to try to build a stable coalition in Gauteng, but could not resolve the tension between them.

items.h: Coalition government negotiations: what to watch
items.s: As the horse trading began, Wiener set out what to watch for as parties negotiate to form metro and council governments.

items.h: Coalition talks ramp up as parties race to meet the deadline
items.s: On 702’s Midday Report, Wiener covered the race to strike coalition deals before the deadline.

items.h: A coalition emerges for the Gauteng metros and eThekwini
items.s: Wiener noted that a coalition of the ANC, ActionSA, EFF and MK is emerging for the Gauteng metros and eThekwini.

items.h: Joburg burns, politicians bargain
items.s: Haffajee argued that as City Power’s grid buckles and coalition talks heat up, Johannesburg’s voters deserve more than another deal for political survival.

items.h: A week on: what do you think of the coalition talks?
items.s: A week after the elections, Katopodis asked her followers what they now think, knowing what they know about hung councils, coalition talks and the spats between parties.

items.h: Coalition Builder: battle for Joburg, who has the numbers?
items.s: On eNCA, Sussman worked through the numbers for three possible coalitions to govern Johannesburg.

items.h: Sussman warns GNU-style coalitions won’t work in local government
items.s: Sussman warned that coalitions modelled on the national unity government will not work in local councils.

items.h: A four-party deal gives the Gauteng coalition a buffer
items.s: Sussman said the proposed coalition of at least four parties for the Gauteng metros gives it a buffer, so the government does not depend on any single small party.

items.h: Who really won South Africa’s 2026 local government elections?
items.s: In an opinion video, Vabaza traces where the vote went after the ANC lost 14.8 points and the DA gained three, and what that means for the coalition talks.

items.h: Zille and Brink silent on the demand that they step aside
items.s: Newsday reported that Brink, the DA’s Tshwane mayoral candidate, and Helen Zille had not said whether they would step aside to make a DA-ActionSA deal possible.

items.h: The ANC’s first meeting with ActionSA
items.s: Mokonyane posted that Fikile Mbalula had led an ANC delegation in a courtesy meeting with ActionSA to reflect on the elections.

items.h: Bhengu: Ramaphosa has stated no preference on Joburg
items.s: Bhengu dismissed reports that Ramaphosa had told the ANC he preferred a Johannesburg coalition without the DA.

items.h: ANC negotiating team denies coalition disagreement in KZN
items.s: Bhengu told SABC News there was no rift between the ANC’s structures and its provincial task team over the KwaZulu-Natal coalition talks.

items.h: The ANC’s preferred Joburg names miss out on council seats
items.s: News24 reports that the ANC’s preferred names for Johannesburg, among them Masuku, Dada Morero and Frank Chikane, did not win council seats.

items.h: Morero on the ANC’s coalition framework
items.s: Before the vote, Morero told eNCA the ANC’s coalition framework puts service delivery, residents’ concerns and respect for the Constitution first.

items.h: Morero on who calls the coalition shots, and being Joburg’s last ANC mayor
items.s: Casting his special vote, Morero answered questions on who calls the ANC’s coalition shots in Johannesburg and whether he would be the city’s last ANC mayor.

items.h: Trollip says it’s up to the DA to break the coalition standoff
items.s: Trollip, once made Nelson Mandela Bay mayor by a coalition and later removed by one, told BizNews it is up to the DA to break the standoff.

items.h: Trollip on DA arrogance and building coalitions that work
items.s: Trollip spoke to News24 about what he sees as DA arrogance, and how to build coalitions that work.

items.h: Stop the fearmongering, it’s not democracy
items.s: Wessels criticised the fearmongering he said was used during the campaign, calling it anti-democratic, as the FF Plus prepared to play kingmaker in hung councils.

items.h: ‘Vote for dignity,’ urges the EFF’s Joburg candidate
items.s: On election day, Mofokeng urged Johannesburg voters to turn out despite their despondency.

items.h: EFF podcast: an uncensored conversation with Julius Malema
items.s: Gcilishe hosted Malema on the EFF podcast for an open conversation, with no questions off the table, as the coalition talks continued.

items.h: MK will not rescue parties rejected by voters
items.s: Duduzane Zuma said MK would not rescue parties that voters had rejected, as coalition talks loomed over hung KwaZulu-Natal councils.

items.h: Duduzane Zuma answers eight key questions as MK fights for a place in government
items.s: He said there would be no political lifelines and no coalitions just for the sake of it.

items.h: Omarjee speaks to Mashaba on ActionSA’s negotiations
items.s: Omarjee interviewed Herman Mashaba about ActionSA’s coalition negotiations and its demands about the DA’s mayoral candidates.

items.h: Coalitions: the ANC’s four options
items.s: Omarjee set out four coalition paths open to the ANC, including letting MK govern alone in some councils.

items.h: Ramaphosa urges ANC to avoid DA in Johannesburg coalition
items.s: Tandwa reported, citing unnamed insiders, that Ramaphosa told a closed ANC meeting to explore a Johannesburg coalition without the DA.

items.h: Why did DA-ActionSA coalition talks collapse in Gauteng?
items.s: Tandwa explained how the dispute over Zille’s mayoral bid, and ActionSA’s demand for an equal share of mayoral committee seats, broke the DA-ActionSA talks.

items.h: An attitude problem that snatches defeat from the jaws of victory
items.s: Sefara argues that Zille’s communication style and past remarks isolate her from potential coalition partners.

items.h: Is Zille too strange to build a coalition?
items.s: Recalling a personal encounter with Zille, Steinberg wondered whether her temperament suits coalition building.

items.h: Zille disputes Steinberg’s account
items.s: Zille replied on X that Jonny Steinberg must have been at a different event, disputing his account of their encounter.

items.h: A game of musical chairs: performance over personalities in coalition politics
items.s: Vabaza backs Zille and the DA and argues for performance agreements and published coalition deals. He also describes Sizwe Mpofu-Walsh’s idea of a DA-ANC-ActionSA grand agreement over the metros.

items.h: Gayton McKenzie’s post-election analysis
items.s: Hogg interviewed PA leader Gayton McKenzie on the morning the ANC’s national executive met to decide its coalition path.

items.h: Michael Beaumont on ActionSA’s coalition hand and the DA standoff
items.s: Hogg interviewed ActionSA’s Michael Beaumont about the DA standoff and the talks with the ANC.

items.h: Zille vs Mashaba: the egos shaping Joburg’s coalition talks
items.s: Makhanya wrote about how the egos of Helen Zille and Herman Mashaba are shaping the Johannesburg talks.

items.h: Is Mashaba’s stance personal, or a calculation?
items.s: Dawes asked whether Mashaba’s reluctance to be the junior partner in a Zille-led Joburg coalition has less to do with personal animus than with a calculation.

items.h: Coalition marriages failing
items.s: Perlman’s 702 Drive show looked at why coalition marriages fail.

items.h: Coalition talks in Joburg continue
items.s: McIver spoke to journalist Ferial Haffajee about the continuing coalition talks in Johannesburg.

items.h: DA takes over Joburg
items.s: An episode of Podcast and Chill with MacG led on the DA topping the vote in Johannesburg.

items.h: Let’s be Frank: coalition talks are underway
items.s: On Be Frank with Mac, MacG turned to the coalition talks, arguing that South Africa faces a basic crisis of trust in the people who govern it.

items.h: Prince Mashele on Mashaba, Zille and the deal that could decide Joburg
items.s: Before the vote, Mashaba and Zille’s rivalry and the deal it could take to govern Johannesburg were the focus of Mashele’s BizNews interview.

items.h: ANC could fall below 15% in 2029, Prince Mashele predicts
items.s: Mashele predicted the ANC could fall below 15% in the 2029 national election, blaming corruption, incompetence and arrogance for its decline.

items.h: ActionSA and the DA should form coalitions
items.s: On Vutha FM, Mashele argued that a coalition between ActionSA and the DA is the only viable way forward for Gauteng’s metros.

items.h: Calls from both sides over the Joburg talks
items.s: Mashele said people from both ActionSA and the DA had called him, asking him to help bring the two parties together in the Johannesburg talks.

items.h: Mashaba alleges the DA tried to buy his support
items.s: In an interview with IOL, Mashaba said the DA had offered him money for his 2029 campaign, that he would not work with Helen Zille or Cilliers Brink, and that the DA’s latest offer was the last straw. The DA declined to respond to the claim.

items.h: Hill-Lewis calls ActionSA’s demand over Zille ‘extortion’
items.s: Speaking to SABC News, Hill-Lewis set out the DA’s final offer, with ActionSA running Tshwane and the DA running Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni, and called ActionSA’s demand that Zille be dropped extortion.

items.h: ActionSA is 90 to 95% of the way to a deal with the ANC, EFF and MK
items.s: Beaumont told SABC News the deal would make Mashaba Johannesburg mayor and keep Nasiphi Moya in Tshwane, but that nothing was signed yet and ActionSA’s senate would decide on Sunday evening, 22 November.

items.h: Inside the ANC’s KZN revolt against the MK Party deal
items.s: Not said in public. News24, citing sources, reports that Mbalula is pushing the MK deal on KwaZulu-Natal while the province’s ANC leaders lean towards an ANC-DA-IFP coalition, ahead of a national executive meeting on Monday.

items.h: ‘Take 30 and give us nine’: Malema’s Limpopo proposal
items.s: On the EFF’s podcast, Malema proposed that of Limpopo’s 39 hung councils, the ANC lead 30 and the EFF nine. Sunday World reports the ANC instead chose the DA as its main partner in the province.

items.h: Mashaba set for Joburg mayoralty as ANC, ActionSA, MK and EFF seal metro pact
items.s: Haffajee reported that the ANC, ActionSA, MK and EFF will form the core of the governments in Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni, with Mashaba likely to be inaugurated as Johannesburg mayor this week. The ANC wants to keep the finance portfolio, and the deal still had to be confirmed by a special meeting of the ANC’s national executive committee on Monday.

items.h: City of Joburg to hold first council meeting after local polls
items.s: Beaumont told EWN the council would most likely be adjourned to Wednesday or so to elect a mayor, with the swearing-in of 270 councillors likely to take all day and evening. EWN reported that the coalition agreement is likely to be signed on Tuesday.

items.h: DA’s Hill-Lewis and ActionSA’s Beaumont offer sharply differing takes on coalition politics
items.s: On 702, Manyathela interviewed Geordin Hill-Lewis and Michael Beaumont about their rival plans for Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni. Hill-Lewis defended the DA’s offer for the ANC to lead about 93 hung councils; Beaumont called the DA’s Gauteng offer “a smash and grab”.

items.h: Hill-Lewis: “The power of the deal is in its simplicity”
items.s: Hill-Lewis told 702 that under the DA’s proposal the ANC would lead about 93 municipalities, the DA about 24 and the IFP roughly 20. He said the Gauteng metros were the biggest obstacle, that he had spoken to Ramaphosa the night before, and that the ANC might still reject the deal.

items.h: Beaumont: the DA’s Gauteng offer is “a smash and grab”
items.s: Beaumont told 702 the DA did not meet ActionSA at any point until Thursday last week, and that its offer was confidence-and-supply rather than power-sharing. He said talks with the ANC and others had made substantial progress, and called the DA’s approach “GNU 2.0”.

items.h: ActionSA considering giving some PR councillor seats to ANC in hung Gauteng metros
items.s: Beaumont told EWN ActionSA would be amenable to one ANC person per municipality coming into council through an ActionSA PR seat, using a dual-membership provision in ActionSA’s constitution. The ANC won no PR seats in the three metros.

items.h: ANC rejects Mashaba’s PR seat horse-trading offer
items.s: Mashaba told The Citizen the Johannesburg council meeting would go ahead as planned and that the DA was wasting its time. He said the partners would regroup during the week to make a final announcement. The Citizen reports he had offered the ANC PR seats in exchange for an extra mayoral committee post.

items.h: Tshwane coalition talks intensify ahead of Thursday council sitting
items.s: Sussman told Rekord the ANC appeared committed to a four-party arrangement in Tshwane with ActionSA, the EFF and MK, and that ActionSA was unlikely to give up its push to keep Nasiphi Moya as mayor. “ActionSA is on the cusp of big things as a political party,” he said.

items.h: ‘We will never give up on Joburg’: Zille on coalition negotiations
items.s: Zille told eNCA the DA would not seek to delay the council through legal action, that it had made its final offer and would go into opposition if it was rejected. She said talks were not over until each party’s executive ratified its deals.

items.h: ANC negotiators prepare to report to NEC as coalition talks gather pace
items.s: Bhengu said the negotiating team would report to the special NEC meeting, guided by the coalition framework the ANC adopted in 2023, and that any coalition must deliver stable councils and reliable services.

items.h: ANC rejects ActionSA offer to accommodate regional chair Loyiso Masuku as PR councillor
items.s: Beaumont told the Mail & Guardian ActionSA had considered the proposal reasonable because the ANC had made significant concessions in the talks, and that it was for the ANC to decide whether to pursue it.

items.h: DA makes offer to ANC, IFP to co-govern 137 hung municipalities across SA
items.s: Goba reported the DA’s proposal that the party with the most votes in each hung council should lead it, giving the ANC 93 mayors, the DA 24 and the IFP 20. Neither the ANC nor the IFP had accepted it yet.

items.h: ActionSA rejects DA’s coalition offer in hung Gauteng metros
items.s: Goba reported that ActionSA called the DA’s final Gauteng offer an “April Fools’ Day joke”. Beaumont told EWN it would use ActionSA’s votes to install DA mayors in Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni without ActionSA in those governments.

items.h: ActionSA says it doesn’t have a problem working with DA
items.s: Goba reported that ActionSA says its problem is with two DA mayoral candidates, Helen Zille and Cilliers Brink, not the DA itself, and that it will back the DA’s mayoral candidate in Nelson Mandela Bay.

items.h: ActionSA considering giving some PR councillor seats to ANC in hung Gauteng metros
items.s: Goba reported that the ANC won no PR seats in Johannesburg, Tshwane or Ekurhuleni, which could keep regional leaders Loyiso Masuku, Eugene Modise and Doctor Xhakaza out of council, and that ActionSA was considering lending it some of its PR seats.

items.h: Joburg coalition talks begin: Will the DA deliver Zille’s head to Mashaba?
items.s: Mafisa reported that after meeting Geordin Hill-Lewis, Herman Mashaba’s condition for a Gauteng deal was that Helen Zille and Cilliers Brink step aside as mayoral candidates, as he would. Analyst Theo Neethling warned Mashaba risked overplaying his hand.

items.h: ‘Financial markets have no right to dictate coalition negotiations’ – ANC
items.s: Mafisa reported the ANC rejecting claims that the rand’s slide was linked to the coalition talks. Spokesperson Mahlengi Bhengu pointed instead to a stronger dollar and expectations of higher US interest rates.

items.h: Gauteng PR seat roundabout could harm ANC, warns insider
items.s: Mafisa reported a senior Gauteng ANC member warning against taking PR seats from ActionSA. Mashaba told The Citizen the ANC’s deputy mayor candidates would be sworn in as ActionSA PR councillors in return for an extra mayoral committee post, and said the ANC had accepted.

items.h: ANC rejects Mashaba’s PR seat horse-trading offer
items.s: Mafisa reported that, according to a senior Gauteng ANC source, the provincial task team rejected Mashaba’s offer, saying an ANC member who takes it up must choose between the ANC and ActionSA. The SACP said its seats are not available.

items.h: Phakathi says MK party is ready to take over eThekwini
items.s: Voting in uMhlanga, Phakathi told The Citizen MK aimed to win eThekwini outright and fix the city’s water problems within 100 days. Any coalition talks, he said, would be decided by the party nationally.

items.h: MK Party tipped for eThekwini mayor as coalition talks near conclusion
items.s: A source told IOL’s Daily News that at Tuesday’s first council meeting MK is set to take the mayoralty, ActionSA the deputy mayor post and the ANC the speaker, pending final talks. ActionSA’s Zwakele Mncwango said talks were at a sensitive stage.

items.h: ActionSA open to Bongani Baloyi as Mashaba’s deputy mayor in Joburg power deal
items.s: Sunday World reported that MK’s Baloyi, a former DA mayor of Midvaal who left ActionSA in 2023, is in the running to be Mashaba’s deputy in Johannesburg, and that ActionSA is open to it, according to people familiar with the talks. It depends on what the ANC and EFF demand.

items.h: 270 Joburg councillors sworn in, but election of new mayor expected to wait until Thursday
items.s: Reporting from the council chamber, Ramushwana wrote that Mashaba and Zille sat on opposite sides as 270 councillors took their oaths. City manager Floyd Brink said some parties had asked to postpone the mayoral vote.

items.h: ‘DA’s offer is not a proposal but an insult’: ActionSA after coalition talks fail
items.s: Ramushwana reported that the DA and ActionSA met on Thursday night and ended without agreement, each unhappy with the other’s proposal. Mashaba told EWN the DA’s offer was “not a proposal but an insult”.

items.h: MK Party and ANC discuss possible eThekwini coalition
items.s: Ramushwana reported that MK and the ANC were discussing governing eThekwini together with an MK mayor. MK spokesperson Sifiso Mahlangu said the party was leaning towards parties it already has arrangements with.

items.h: Hill-Lewis: DA unlikely to match ANC’s coalition offer to ActionSA
items.s: Ramushwana reported Hill-Lewis saying the DA was unlikely to match the ANC’s offer to ActionSA. Hill-Lewis confirmed some in the DA had informally discussed him swapping places with Zille, but said it was never put to ActionSA.

items.h: Left-wing parties refuse to back ANC-led coalitions that include the DA
items.s: Ramushwana reported that the Council of the Left, a bloc including the EFF, SACP, MK and the Afrika Mayibuye Movement, would not support ANC-led coalitions that include the DA. The bloc briefed the media at the hotel where the ANC’s NEC was meeting.

items.h: DA threatens legal action over Johannesburg council’s inaugural meeting
items.s: Moichela reported that the DA served city manager Floyd Brink a lawyer’s letter asking for the first meeting to be postponed, arguing the legal deadline was 27 November. He reported that MK’s Bongani Baloyi was expected to take the deputy mayor post.

items.h: Mashaba poised for Joburg mayor role as coalition deal takes shape, MK Party in line for deputy
items.s: Moichela reported, citing sources, an unsigned structure with Mashaba as Joburg mayor and MK as deputy, Nasiphi Moya keeping Tshwane with an EFF deputy, and the ANC leading Ekurhuleni with ActionSA as deputy.

items.h: ANC offers ActionSA Joburg and Tshwane mayoral seats, keeps Ekurhuleni in coalition deal
items.s: Moichela reported, citing sources, that the ANC had offered ActionSA the Johannesburg and Tshwane mayoralties while keeping Ekurhuleni. An ANC insider said the party was negotiating in line with its poor election result.

items.h: Smaller parties rally behind Herman Mashaba for Joburg mayor as coalition talks near crunch point
items.s: Moichela reported sources saying smaller parties in Johannesburg favoured Mashaba for mayor because of his record in office, while noting it was not clear that all smaller parties shared that view.

items.h: Zille, Mashaba officially sworn in as Joburg councillors
items.s: Ramushwana reported that all 270 councillors, including Zille, Mashaba and MK’s 15, had taken their oaths, with 21 parties now in the council. City manager Floyd Brink said the DA had asked for the election of the mayor to be postponed.

items.h: eThekwini insists council meeting will go ahead despite KZN Cogta’s postponement order
items.s: Goba reported that KZN Cogta’s Scelo Duma had told 13 hung municipalities, eThekwini among them, to postpone Tuesday’s first council meetings, but eThekwini spokesperson Senzelwe Mzila said its meeting would still go ahead.

items.h: The ANC is being destroyed by its splinters and allies
items.s: Van Onselen estimated the ANC lost about 25 points in predominantly black metro voting districts, with roughly 14 going to MK, 10 to ActionSA and 5 to the DA. The Common Sense, which published his figures, argued that this complicates the ANC’s choice of coalition partners.

items.h: Gareth van Onselen on the metro races that could redraw SA politics
items.s: Before the vote, van Onselen talked Alec Hogg through Johannesburg’s polling divide, turnout risks and the coalition battles likely in the metros.

items.h: When the horse trading is over, what coalitions will govern Gauteng?
items.s: Berkowitz argues two of the DA, ANC and ActionSA will end up running Gauteng, and that an ANC–ActionSA pact looks likelier: it needs more partners, but more parties, including the EFF, SACP and MK, are willing to join it. ActionSA is the kingmaker in Ekurhuleni.

items.h: ANC bleeding from ‘a thousand cuts’ as smaller parties reshape coalitions
items.s: Speaking to Inside Politic, Berkowitz said the ANC was losing support on many fronts at once, to ActionSA, the DA, the UDM, the SACP and local movements.

items.h: Four eThekwini polls show MK’s possible paths to power
items.s: Before the vote, Berkowitz compared four eThekwini polls. MK came first in all of them, and the opposition parties reached a majority in only two of the four scenarios.

items.h: ANC faces coalition scramble as control of key metros slips away
items.s: Simelane reported that, with councils due to sit within 14 days, the ANC had lost the lead in Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni to the DA and in eThekwini to MK, leaving it to choose between coalition deals and opposition.

items.h: ANC NEC to decide coalition strategy as DA meets ActionSA
items.s: Simelane reported that the ANC’s NEC would meet on 12 November to set its Gauteng coalition strategy while the DA and ActionSA held their own talks, with ActionSA’s support likely to decide who governs.

items.h: FF Plus fails to broker DA–ActionSA coalition as Gauteng talks stall
items.s: Simelane reported that the FF Plus’s Corné Mulder held one-on-one talks to ease tensions between Helen Zille and Herman Mashaba, but could not broker a DA–ActionSA deal, while ANC-led options gained support.

items.h: DA offers ANC 93 mayoralties in 137 councils as ActionSA rejects Gauteng proposal
items.s: Simelane reported the DA’s written “stability framework”, signed by Ashor Sarupen and sent to Fikile Mbalula, which would extend the GNU to hung councils, and ActionSA’s rejection of a separate DA offer for the Gauteng metros.

items.h: New results: coalition madness coming, metros facing massive battles
items.s: As results firmed up, Corder went through how coalitions could take shape in South Africa’s cities, and looked at the rise of the right wing in the country’s politics.

items.h: ANC to cut out the DA?
items.s: Corder discussed reports that the ANC was debating internally whether to drop the DA and partner with ActionSA in councils across the country.

items.h: ANC fights over DA: Ramaphosa vs Mashatile, DA vs ActionSA
items.s: Corder covered a weekend of talks in which the ANC struggled to commit to the DA, while Herman Mashaba claimed victory for ActionSA in Gauteng.

items.h: GNU breakup? Will an ANC–ActionSA alliance end the DA in national government?
items.s: Corder asked whether the DA would walk away from the unity government as an ANC–ActionSA coalition in Gauteng began to look more concrete.

items.h: “The ANC will be dead”: ANC decides today on DA, ActionSA, MK, EFF
items.s: Corder said the talks had reached the sharp end, with the ANC seemingly certain to align broadly with ActionSA, though some in the ANC fear the deal will badly hurt the party.

items.h: Post-election analysis on Podcast and Chill with MacG
items.s: Vabaza joined MacG and Sol Phenduka as the show’s political analyst to go through what the election revealed, the EFF’s decline, the battle for power in Johannesburg, how the Joburg coalitions could fall and whether the ANC can rebuild before 2029.

items.h: Coalition negotiations: new Joburg mayor now expected to be elected Friday
items.s: Ramushwana reported that parties were in the final stages of coalition talks and that Johannesburg’s mayor is now expected to be elected on Friday, after councillors agreed on Monday to postpone the vote. Ekurhuleni’s council sits on Wednesday and Tshwane’s on Thursday.

items.h: eThekwini to go ahead with inaugural council meeting despite KZN Cogta directive
items.s: Goba reported that eThekwini would hold its first council meeting on Tuesday even though KZN Cogta had told 13 municipalities to postpone, without giving a reason beyond “continuing engagements”. All 224 councillors are to be sworn in and a speaker, mayor, deputy mayor and chief whip elected; KwaZulu-Natal’s 35 hung councils have no finalised coalition pacts.

items.h: Podcast and Chill: coalition talks update
items.s: MacG and Sol Phenduka’s Monday episode of Podcast and Chill included an update on the coalition talks, alongside the week’s entertainment news.

items.h: Crunch time for coalition talks
items.s: With councils starting to elect mayors and speakers before the 14-day deadline, Mpofu-Walsh went through the latest in the talks and what to expect in the big metros, asking whether the DA’s share of the vote entitles it to govern and questioning its record in government.

items.h: The truth about the ANC coalition they don’t want you to question
items.s: Mashele joined DJ Sbu on The Hustlers Corner SA podcast for a full episode on the ANC’s coalition deals.

items.h: ‘No party off limits’, say rivals, as coalition talks loom
items.s: Dooms told Sowetan the elections were likely to produce more coalition governments than ever before, with smaller parties and independent candidates potentially holding the balance of power in municipalities across the country.

items.h: DA’s Ekurhuleni breakthrough exposes an uncomfortable truth about the ANC
items.s: Speaking to CapeTalk, Dooms said the ANC’s dramatic decline was a defining feature of the results. The DA had grown in Ekurhuleni, she said, but its improved position was largely the result of the ANC losing support, and the vote reflected disillusionment with incumbents rather than an endorsement of any one party.

items.h: Why Herman Mashaba holds the cards in DA coalition talks
items.s: Dooms told Kaya 959 that the ANC appears to see a deal with the DA as a risk because of how its own supporters feel about it, and that the 14-day window may not prevent a revolving door of mayors. She called the DA’s outreach to MK, a party it had described as unconstitutional, one of the surprises of the talks, and said MK had learnt to respect its voters’ wishes.

items.h: Post-election analysis on Podcast and Chill
items.s: Co-hosting with MacG, Phenduka went through what the election revealed, the EFF’s decline and the fight for Johannesburg with the show’s political analyst Zimasa Vabaza.

items.h: Podcast and Chill: coalition talks update
items.s: Phenduka co-hosted Monday’s Podcast and Chill with MacG, which included an update on the coalition talks.

items.h: How Mashaba and ‘AuctionSA’ betrayed their ‘gatvol’ voters
items.s: In his weekly column, Basson argues that Herman Mashaba chose revenge politics over putting the wishes of ActionSA’s “gatvol” voters first.

items.h: Joburg mayor vote pushed to Friday as coalition talks continue
items.s: With Reitumetse Pilane and Naledi Mashishi, Simelane reported Daily Maverick’s live coverage of Johannesburg’s first council sitting: councillors were sworn in, the election of the speaker, mayor and deputy mayor was postponed to Friday, and parties were expected to sign their agreement on Tuesday, with issues still outstanding.

items.h: Ramaphosa faces tough ANC unity test in coalition talks
items.s: Before Monday’s NEC, Omarjee reported that two Luthuli House sources said sidelining the DA for pacts with ActionSA, the EFF and MK had sparked fierce debate, but opponents of the “done deal” expected to be in the minority. The sources said Ramaphosa himself had told the party to avoid coalitions with the DA and to treat one as a last resort.

items.h: What happened to Cyril Ramaphosa?
items.s: Steinberg argues that Ramaphosa spending one of the most important weeks of his presidency in California is a sign of his waning power.

items.h: IFP pushes for countrywide coalition partnerships
items.s: Goba reported that the IFP wants coalition partners across the country rather than deals in isolated municipalities.

items.h: Zille calls for electoral reform to stop small parties ‘making government unstable’
items.s: Speaking to News24 before Johannesburg’s first sitting, Zille said the DA had submitted a private member’s bill for a 2% vote threshold for any party to be represented in legislatures and councils, calling it undemocratic that parties with under 1% can shape who governs. The DA has 91 of Johannesburg’s 270 seats.

items.h: The ANC lost the metros. Tony Leon says it still holds most of the cards
items.s: On Conversations with Gabriel, Tony Leon told Makin why the ANC still holds most of the cards in coalition talks despite its electoral collapse.

items.h: Voters rejected the ANC. ActionSA wants to bring it back
items.s: On Conversations with Gabriel, FF Plus leader Corné Mulder told Makin that ActionSA is making the wrong calculation by negotiating with the ANC after voters rejected it.

items.h: Does it even matter who the ANC picks?
items.s: As the ANC decides who to govern with, Makin and Marius Roodt discussed why a deal with MK and the EFF may suit the party better than the alternatives.

items.h: ANC NEC to provide direction on how to approach coalition talks
items.s: Maseko previewed the ANC NEC meeting due the next day, which was to give direction on how the party approaches coalition talks.

items.h: MK Party and DA meet for coalition talks
items.s: Reporting from Waterfall, near Midrand, where the ANC was meeting to decide how it would approach coalition negotiations with other parties.

items.h: DA and MK Party conclude coalition talks
items.s: Maseko reported live as the MK Party and the DA appeared to wrap up their coalition meeting at Waterfall in Johannesburg.

items.h: Coalition deals continue in Gauteng
items.s: The ANC, EFF, ActionSA and MK Party met that morning to finalise their talks on forming coalitions in Gauteng; Maseko updated from the meeting.

items.h: ANC, EFF, ActionSA and MKP meet to discuss working together
items.s: Maseko spoke to ActionSA and MK Party representatives after the two parties met to discuss coalitions in municipalities across the country.

items.h: Deadline approaches for constitution of councils
items.s: With the deadline for councils to sit approaching, Maseko unpacked the latest negotiations; the ANC, seen as kingmaker, was expected to announce outcomes on Friday.

items.h: We’ll approach negotiations with humility: DA’s Cilliers Brink
items.s: Giokos interviewed the DA’s Tshwane mayoral candidate Cilliers Brink, who said the party would go into coalition negotiations with humility and openness.

items.h: Political parties explore coalition possibilities in Gauteng
items.s: Giokos reported on the coalition negotiations and the latest developments in Gauteng’s three metros.

items.h: Coalition negotiations over Gauteng metros
items.s: A further update from Giokos on the talks over who will govern Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni.

items.h: The DA’s big win comes with strings attached
items.s: Bruce called ActionSA’s position in Johannesburg and Tshwane the biggest coalition problem to come out of the 4 November elections.

items.h: ActionSA’s rise complicates Gauteng coalition talks
items.s: Bruce wrote on how ActionSA’s rise complicates the coalition talks in Gauteng’s metros.

items.h: ActionSA eyes Joburg mayoralty with ANC support
items.s: Bruce argued that Herman Mashaba’s best route to the Johannesburg mayoralty runs through ANC support, since Mashaba has said he won’t serve under a DA mayor.

items.h: ActionSA at the crossroads — real governance or just another ego-driven party?
items.s: Grootes argued that ActionSA’s future depends on whether it can outlast Herman Mashaba and become a party built on more than one person.

items.h: The smoke and mirrors of the coalition talks
items.s: Grootes wrote that the ANC and ActionSA staged a publicised first meeting, and that the arrangement could help Mashaba ahead of the 2029 elections.

items.h: EFF ready to put service delivery ahead of politics in coalition talks
items.s: EFF secretary-general Marshall Dlamini told Masuabi the party would work with parties it opposes nationally, but wants positions and a role in running municipalities in return.

items.h: Power struggle begins: Coalition negotiations intensify across 126 hung municipalities
items.s: With colleagues, Masuabi reported that 126 of 195 declared councils had no outright majority, almost double the number after 2021, with seven of eight metros heading for coalitions.

items.h: ActionSA ‘still far from coalition deal in Joburg and Tshwane’
items.s: ActionSA chair Michael Beaumont told Sunday World the party was far from a deal: posts on mayoral committees, council seats and a programme for each city were still unsettled.

items.h: ANC’s Adolph Marema tipped for Joburg speaker in ActionSA coalition deal
items.s: Masuabi reported that the ANC’s Adolph Marema had emerged as frontrunner for council speaker as the ANC, ActionSA, EFF, MK and SACP moved closer to a deal making Mashaba mayor.

items.h: ANC offers ActionSA mayorship deal to bypass DA
items.s: Maeko reported that the ANC had proposed a coalition making Herman Mashaba mayor of Johannesburg, keeping Nasiphi Moya in Tshwane and giving the ANC Ekurhuleni, leaving the DA out.

items.h: Could MK Party claim deputy mayor of Joburg role?
items.s: ActionSA and the ANC edged towards a deal but needed EFF and MK backing for majorities; the proposals discussed had MK taking Joburg’s deputy mayor post.

items.h: ANC NEC mulls competing KZN coalition proposals with eye on Durban
items.s: The ANC’s national leadership was weighing several KwaZulu-Natal coalition proposals; one would pair the ANC, IFP, DA and a ratepayers’ association, with about 54% of eThekwini’s seats.

items.h: Coalition talks delay SA council meetings amid legal challenges
items.s: Maeko reported that legal challenges and party disputes were delaying council inaugurations in key cities, with a directive postponing council meetings.

items.h: JJ Tabane: Can South Africa’s coalitions deliver real change?
items.s: In an interview with Truth Report, Tabane examined the ANC’s election losses, its record on accountability and the coalition negotiations.

items.h: Coalition special with JJ Tabane
items.s: Tabane hosted a Sunday World panel of political analysts, including Qaanitah Hunter and Brutus Malada, to debate the coalition negotiations taking place behind closed doors.

items.h: Will Cyril resign now? Is ActionSA about to betray its voters?
items.s: With 138 hung councils and 14 days to form governments, Shepherd went through the tense coalition talks after the ANC fell to 30%.

items.h: Thabo Mbeki is mad with the ANC; Malema to sue Helen Zille?
items.s: Coalition talks were under way in 138 councils; Shepherd discussed how deals with ActionSA could secure the Gauteng metros and the ANC centralising talks under Fikile Mbalula.

items.h: Who will govern where?
items.s: Shepherd looked at ANC–DA cooperation facing resistance over BEE and transformation, and at alliances with ActionSA, the EFF and MK that could decide Gauteng’s metros.

items.h: The great betrayal of ActionSA? DA coalition with the MK Party?
items.s: With talks stalled, Shepherd covered ActionSA reporting progress with the ANC in Gauteng and Mashaba demanding the DA remove Helen Zille as its candidate.

items.h: What now for the coalitions?
items.s: Talks remained unsettled: no confirmed Gauteng deal, ActionSA rejecting DA mayoral candidates and disputed ANC–MK talks in KwaZulu-Natal.

items.h: Herman Mashaba caught lying?
items.s: Shepherd contrasted Mashaba’s 2021 promise that ActionSA wouldn’t help the ANC take Joburg with the party’s talks with the ANC five years later.

items.h: The great betrayal of ActionSA appears to be complete
items.s: The ANC and ActionSA had a tentative deal on Tshwane and Ekurhuleni, with Johannesburg unresolved and EFF and MK support possibly needed.

items.h: Helen Zille quits; ActionSA sells its votes to the ANC?
items.s: ActionSA and the DA had yet to meet formally, with ActionSA reportedly demanding the DA drop Helen Zille and Cilliers Brink.

items.h: Coalition chaos everywhere
items.s: DA–ActionSA talks had collapsed over Zille and power-sharing; an ActionSA–ANC deal could make Mashaba mayor and give the ANC Ekurhuleni, but needs EFF and MK support.

items.h: Herman gives the ANC the purse strings?
items.s: Shepherd reported the ANC wants control of city finances in return for backing ActionSA mayors in Joburg and Tshwane, and that Mashaba defended the demand.

items.h: No Helen, you do not have to form a government in 14 days
items.s: Wyatt explained the rules for forming coalitions after the election, arguing that media and politicians misread the 14-day timeline.

items.h: DA suddenly in coalition talks with EFF and MK
items.s: Wyatt looked at the DA’s strategy after winning over 1.1 million new voters, against its earlier refusals to enter coalitions with the EFF and MK.

items.h: DA in coalition talks with EFF and MK (Night Owls)
items.s: A Night Owls episode on the DA’s talks with the EFF and MK.

items.h: No coalitions with EFF or MK (so said the DA)
items.s: A Chris Wyatt Reports episode on the DA’s earlier pledge not to work with the EFF or MK.

items.h: ANC–ActionSA coalition of incompetence? (Night Owls)
items.s: A Night Owls episode on a possible ANC–ActionSA coalition.

items.h: South Africa’s coalition mess: 14 days later
items.s: Fourteen days after the election, Wyatt examined the uncertainty as parties negotiated and councils prepared to sit.

items.h: “ActionSA will never go into a coalition with ANC” — oops, they did
items.s: Wyatt set Mashaba’s pledge that ActionSA would never enter a coalition with the ANC against the party’s current talks with it.

items.h: Helen Zille reportedly concedes defeat in Johannesburg mayor race
items.s: Wyatt reacted to reports that Helen Zille had conceded the Johannesburg mayoral race.

items.h: Municipal coalition progress in South Africa
items.s: A Chris Wyatt Reports update on progress in municipal coalition talks.

items.h: Mashaba vs the reality: a coalition of chaos
items.s: Wyatt went through calls for Mashaba to step down and tensions involving ActionSA and Julius Malema, reviewing a column by Adriaan Basson.

items.h: South Africa’s new coalitions may have just been built by one man
items.s: Cohen asked whether party leaders hold real power in the coalition talks, or whether one wealthy backer could decide South Africa’s political future.

items.h: Coalition standoff: one party is the clear winner in the ANC–DA–ActionSA negotiations
items.s: Doing the coalition maths on the metros, Cohen argued one of the three parties holds the clear edge, particularly ahead of the next national election.

items.h: Iran wants this governing coalition to rule over South Africa’s municipalities
items.s: Cohen looked at foreign actors watching the coalition talks, arguing Iran may have a vested interest in how they unfold.

items.h: ActionSA want the Freedom Front Plus to mediate negotiations with the DA
items.s: Cohen covered ActionSA wanting the FF Plus to mediate its talks with the DA, asking whether it could be a breakthrough.

items.h: DA and ANC enter Limpopo coalition
items.s: Cohen went through the DA and ANC entering a coalition in Limpopo, and what it says about the national talks.

items.h: DA submits final offer to ActionSA and they’ve already responded
items.s: After the DA broke its silence on the talks, Cohen went through its final offer to ActionSA and ActionSA’s responses on social media.

items.h: Coalition chaos, what voters really want: Gareth Cliff unfiltered
items.s: Cohen spoke to Gareth Cliff about coalition chaos, what voters want, and the DA–ActionSA stand-off.

items.h: Can the GNU teach parties about governing SA’s municipalities?
items.s: On 702 Breakfast, Bingwa asked what the national unity government could teach parties about governing municipalities through coalitions.

items.h: Coalition horse-trading: who will govern South Africa’s metros?
items.s: A 702 Breakfast segment on the horse-trading over who will govern South Africa’s metros.

items.h: Coalition talks: Is ActionSA the kingmaker in Gauteng’s metros?
items.s: Bingwa and analyst Sandile Swana unpacked the talks in Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni: ActionSA’s kingmaker role, the dispute over mayoral candidates and whether the ANC or DA can win its support.

items.h: Mashaba hints at possible coalition governments without DA in Gauteng
items.s: ActionSA president Herman Mashaba spoke to Bingwa about the coalition negotiations in Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni.

items.h: The battle for South Africa’s hung councils
items.s: Bingwa spoke to UCT’s Prof Richard Calland about the Johannesburg talks: 270 councillors sworn in, but still no mayor, speaker or mayoral committee.

items.h: ActionSA to negotiate with DA against Mashaba’s wishes
items.s: Lubelwana discussed Michael Beaumont pressing ahead with talks with the DA against Herman Mashaba’s wishes.

items.h: ANC to dump DA or continue?
items.s: On the ANC at a crossroads over whether to keep working with the DA.

items.h: DA wants to work with EFF and MKP

events.h: Joburg will elect its mayor on Friday as parties finish their deal
events.dek: All 270 councillors were sworn in on Monday, but the election of a mayor, deputy mayor and speaker now waits until Friday, 27 November. The ANC, ActionSA, EFF and MK deal that would make Mashaba mayor is in its final stages but still to be signed.
brief: Helen Zille, Herman Mashaba and the rest of the 270 councillors were sworn in on Monday
Parties agreed to postpone the election of the speaker, mayor and deputy mayor; EWN now expects the mayor to be elected on Friday, 27 November
Ekurhuleni’s council sits on Wednesday and Tshwane’s on Thursday, EWN reports

The deal would make Mashaba mayor; IOL and Sunday World report MK’s Bongani Baloyi is expected to be his deputy
sec: An early opening for Zille
On 4 November, Pieter du Toit wrote that a Zille-led city working with the ANC’s moderates was not far-fetched, though it would be very hard to negotiate.
Zille becomes the sticking point

On election night, Herman Mashaba told Clement Manyathela on 702 that he would not negotiate with a DA team that included Zille. On 17 November, Michael Beaumont named the two parties’ Gauteng mayoral candidates as the sticking point. The next day DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis told Manyathela the party would not drop Zille and would accept opposition if it came to that, while Beaumont called the ANC’s offer attractive.
Swap talk

On 18 November, Hill-Lewis dismissed as dramatic the reports that he had offered to step down as Cape Town mayor, a claim Manyathela put to him on 702 the same day. Two days later Beaumont posted a video arguing that Zille had broken a working coalition in Johannesburg before and would not get a second chance.
Zille concedes

On 18 November, Zille told DA caucus members the die seemed to be cast and the party should prepare for opposition. She said she believed an ANC-ActionSA-EFF-MK coalition would be unstable, but that the DA could still help Johannesburg have a working government. The DA said this was not its official position.
ActionSA moves on

Mashaba told the Mail & Guardian that talks with the DA stalled because it would not drop Zille and Cilliers Brink, and that ActionSA was drafting an agreement with the other parties. Adriaan Basson wrote that the party with the most votes in the city was heading for opposition, and Beaumont said ActionSA was set to take over in Johannesburg.
Decision day

On 21 November, Beaumont told SABC News that ActionSA was 90 to 95% of the way to a deal with the ANC, EFF and MK that would make Mashaba mayor of Johannesburg and keep Nasiphi Moya in Tshwane, though nothing was signed and ActionSA’s senate would decide on Sunday evening. The same day Hill-Lewis made the DA’s final offer and called ActionSA’s demand that Zille be dropped extortion, while Mashaba told IOL the DA had tried to buy his support, which the DA declined to answer.
Monday, 23 November

On Sunday, Inside Politics reported that Mashaba had made himself available for mayor ahead of a council sitting on Monday, while a source said no formal agreement had yet been reached. On Monday morning, Ferial Haffajee reported in Daily Maverick that the ANC, ActionSA, MK and EFF would form the core of the governments in Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni, and that Mashaba was likely to be inaugurated this week. She reported that the ANC wants to keep the finance portfolio and that the arrangement still had to be confirmed by a special meeting of the ANC’s national executive committee on Monday. The National reported that the council was due to sit at 1pm at the Constance Connie Bapela Council Chamber in Braamfontein, and that it was uncertain whether a mayor would be elected at the sitting. Beaumont told EWN the council would most likely be adjourned to Wednesday or so for the mayoral election, and EWN reported that the coalition agreement is likely to be signed on Tuesday. eNCA reported that the ANC’s national executive committee would meet on Monday to consider a report from its negotiating team and give it further direction. Later in the morning, The National reported that the DA had asked the city to postpone the sitting and had threatened legal action after city manager Floyd Brink rejected an earlier request, arguing that the first meeting need not be held before 27 November. It put the combined strength of the ANC, ActionSA, EFF and MK at 137 seats, against the 136 needed, and said MK was expected to take the deputy mayor post, with the agreement expected to be signed on Tuesday.
Tuesday, 24 November

Early on Tuesday, Alpha Ramushwana reported for EWN that parties were in the final stages of their coalition negotiations and that Johannesburg’s new mayor is now expected to be elected on Friday. He reported that Ekurhuleni’s council will sit on Wednesday and Tshwane’s only on Thursday.

sec: Why the ANC has no PR seats

The ANC won more wards than any other party in the three metros, so its ward seats already exceeded its share of the vote and it was given no PR seats. EWN reports that its regional leaders who stood as PR candidates, including Johannesburg chair Loyiso Masuku, Tshwane chair Eugene Modise and Ekurhuleni leader Doctor Xhakaza, could miss out.
The offer
Michael Beaumont told EWN that ActionSA would be amenable to one ANC person per municipality coming through an ActionSA PR seat, using a dual-membership provision in its constitution.
Reported: the ANC says no

A senior Gauteng ANC source told The Citizen the provincial task team rejected the offer, saying an ANC member who takes it up must choose between the ANC and ActionSA. The SACP said its seats are not open to any party, and that lists already gazetted cannot be changed.
Why ActionSA offered

Michael Beaumont told the Mail & Guardian ActionSA was willing to accommodate Masuku because the ANC had made significant concessions in the negotiations. “It is for them to say whether they pursue it or not,” he said.

events.dek: The DA’s nationwide framework would have the ANC lead 93 hung councils, the DA 24 and the IFP 20. A separate Gauteng offer, which ActionSA rejected, would have let ActionSA run Tshwane while the DA led Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni.

sec: The numbers

Daily Maverick reports that the DA’s “stability framework”, sent to ANC secretary-general Fikile Mbalula on 20 November and signed by Ashor Sarupen, gives the ANC 93 mayoralties, the DA 24 and the IFP 20, subject to the IFP agreeing. The largest party among the partners in each council would lead it. Nineteen councils where the ANC and SACP already have a majority would be left out.
Gauteng: an offer ActionSA would not take

Under the DA’s separate Gauteng offer, Nasiphi Moya would stay mayor of Tshwane while the DA led Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni, as a confidence-and-supply arrangement. ActionSA said it would have had to back DA governments in two metros without seats on their mayoral committees, and would not support a Helen Zille mayoralty.
On 702

Geordin Hill-Lewis told Clement Manyathela that “the power of the deal is in its simplicity”, that the Gauteng metros are the biggest obstacle, and that he had spoken to Ramaphosa the night before. Michael Beaumont said the DA had not met ActionSA until last Thursday and called its offer “a smash and grab”.

events.h: In public, Ramaphosa asks for good faith. In private, insiders say he wants the DA kept out of Joburg

sec: What he said in public

At the IEC results announcement on 8 November, Ramaphosa said hung councils should not be read as a failure of democracy, and urged parties to negotiate in good faith rather than fight over positions and power. In his weekly newsletter the next day, he said councillors must find common ground from the start so councils can begin working.
What insiders say he said

On 11 November the Sunday Times reported, citing unnamed insiders, that Ramaphosa told a closed ANC meeting to explore a Johannesburg coalition without the DA. ANC spokesperson Mahlengi Bhengu dismissed claims that he had stated a preference. Preamble has not seen this confirmed on the record.
The NEC decides

Before the meeting, Business Day’s Hajra Omarjee reported Luthuli House sources saying Ramaphosa had told the party to avoid coalitions with the DA and treat one as a last resort, with opponents of the four-party deal expecting to be in the minority. Late on Monday, News24 reported that the national executive committee had handed the power to choose coalition partners to its provinces and regions, which have very different preferences on whom to align with.

events.h: Should one deal settle all eight metros?

sec: The grand-bargain idea

On his SMWX podcast on 7 November, Mpofu-Walsh set out an idea for one coalition arrangement across the country. A clip of him shared on Facebook is titled how the DA, ANC and ActionSA can divide the eight metros. Commentator Sindile Vabaza describes the split as the DA in Johannesburg, Cape Town, Mangaung and Nelson Mandela Bay, the ANC in Ekurhuleni, eThekwini and Buffalo City, and ActionSA in Tshwane. Preamble has the exact split from Vabaza’s account.
Other national formulas

Adriaan Basson argued on 9 November that a DA-ANC deal modelled on the national unity government was the most likely outcome. On 22 November Geordin Hill-Lewis put a different formula to the ANC and IFP: the party with the most votes in each hung council leads it.
A realignment?

By 13 November Mpofu-Walsh was asking whether South Africa is entering a fundamental political realignment, looking at Mashaba and Moya leading Gauteng metros and an MK-IFP arrangement in KwaZulu-Natal.

On 7 November, Dali Mpofu said MK’s near-10% national vote shows voters want parties to cooperate. Any deal, he said, must rest on shared policy and be concluded within 100 days of a council being set up, with MK’s leadership having the final say.
A warning to the ANC
On 12 November, Mpofu warned that the ANC working with parties whose interests oppose its own could lead to its demise, while saying MK did not want the talks to become a slanging match.
Talking to the DA

Around 14 November, Mpofu described MK’s first-ever meeting with the DA as historic, and confirmed that DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis had asked for the talks. But he said MK will focus on like-minded parties. By 19 November, MK’s talks with the ANC, EFF and ActionSA were continuing, including in eThekwini.
A split in the ANC

News24 reports, citing sources, that Fikile Mbalula is pushing the MK deal on KwaZulu-Natal while the province’s ANC leaders lean towards an ANC-DA-IFP coalition, ahead of a national executive meeting on Monday. EWN reports the ANC and MK are expected to discuss sharing power, including in eThekwini, where MK took 38% of the vote.
eThekwini sits

On Tuesday morning, Thabiso Goba reported for EWN that eThekwini would hold its inaugural meeting that day despite the provincial directive, with all 224 councillors to be sworn in and a speaker, mayor, deputy mayor and chief whip on the agenda. eNCA reported that MK, the largest party in the hung council, is in a potentially influential position.

On 702 on 18 November he called the ANC’s offer attractive and said the DA had never really held talks with ActionSA. By 22 November he was pushing back at DA supporters, saying ActionSA serves at the pleasure of no other party and is set to lead Tshwane again and take over in Johannesburg.

events.dek: Adriaan Basson first expected the DA and ANC to copy their national partnership in the councils. By mid-November he was warning that the fight over the cities could bring it down.

sec: Four ways it could go

On 7 November, Basson set out four coalition line-ups that could decide who runs South Africa’s municipalities. On X he named them Ukraine, Lesotho, Rainbow and Ghana, three of them after national flags with the same colours.
GNU 2.0
Two days later he argued that a deal led by the DA and ANC, modelled on the national unity government, was the most likely way the 138 hung councils would be run.
The risk to the national government

By 16 November he was warning that the unity government could collapse if the ANC cut the DA out of city governments. On 21 November, as ANC and MK leaders met in Johannesburg, he asked whether a Doomsday pact was Ramaphosa’s parting shot.
A collision course
On 19 November, Pieter du Toit wrote that the DA and ANC are now on a collision course ahead of the 2029 national election.

pieces.s: DW said the party that once stood for liberation from apartheid is in decline, with voters angry about unemployment, crime and corruption. With 98% counted, the ANC had 31% and the DA almost 25%, and the ANC had lost its majority in six of the eight metros. DW expected the DA to try to form coalitions without the ANC in Pretoria and Johannesburg, while Zuma’s MK led in Durban.

It expected the DA, clearly ahead in Pretoria and Johannesburg, to form coalitions there without the ANC, while MK led in Durban and the DA won Cape Town outright.

pieces.h: ANC suffers historic defeat in South Africa’s local elections
pieces.orig: ANC erleidet historische Niederlage bei Kommunalwahl in Südafrika
pieces.s: The FAZ called it the ANC’s worst result since 1994: under a third of the vote, against more than 45% in 2021, and no outright majority in any big city. It focused on Johannesburg, where the DA came first with 35% against 20% for the ANC and 16% for ActionSA, after a campaign by the German-born Helen Zille that included snorkelling in a pothole. It treats local elections as a pointer to the next national election.

pieces.h: South Africa punishes Mandela’s party in local elections that open a new battle for local power
pieces.orig: Sudáfrica castiga al partido de Mandela en unas municipales que abren una nueva batalla por el poder local
pieces.s: El País reported the ANC on 30.76% and the DA on 24.64%, with MK third on 9.76%, and said the result points to hard bargaining over metros such as Johannesburg and Durban, with the ANC negotiating from its weakest position yet. Parties have 14 days before councils sit, and the number of councils needing coalitions has more than doubled since 2021. It quoted Mbalula calling the result “catastrophic” and saying the honest response is to “go home and put our house in order”.

pieces.h: Mandela’s party suffers a setback in the municipal elections: what comes next for South Africa?
pieces.orig: El partido de Mandela sufre un revés en las elecciones municipales: ¿qué viene ahora en Sudáfrica?
pieces.s: France 24 reported the final result: 30.76% for the ANC, its worst ever, against 24.64% for the DA and 9.76% for MK. With no majority in many cities, Johannesburg included, the ANC and DA must deal with each other or with smaller parties, and the number of councils needing coalitions has more than doubled since 2021. It quoted Ramaphosa saying “the people have spoken”, and Fikile Mbalula calling the result “catastrophic” but saying the ANC would not beg for posts.

pieces.h: Mandela’s party gets its worst result in South Africa’s municipal elections: “The people have spoken”

pieces.s: Infobae led with Ramaphosa saying “the people have spoken” and that their verdict must be respected. It reported the ANC on 30.76%, almost 15 points down on 2021 and without a majority in any of the eight metros, and the DA winning Cape Town outright. Turnout was about 52%, up from 45.7% in 2021, and voters cited water shortages and power cuts, with unemployment at 33.6%.

pieces.h: In South Africa, the ANC has lost the big cities

pieces.s: With counting still under way, Il Post reported that the ANC was losing almost all of South Africa’s biggest cities: about 21% in Pretoria, where it ran third behind the DA and ActionSA, 17% in Johannesburg and under 10% in Cape Town. It linked the losses to crime and failing infrastructure, with frequent water and power cuts, and to a campaign it called lazy and late.

pieces.h: In South Africa the ANC heads for record lows, and the coalition puzzle begins
pieces.orig: In Sudafrica l’Anc verso i minimi storici, scatta rebus coalizioni
pieces.s: Writing from Nairobi, Il Sole 24 Ore reported the ANC heading for about 32% against 24% for the DA, a slide that opens a “puzzle” of local coalitions. It said the result could shake or reshape the national unity government formed with the DA in 2024, and is a new blow to Ramaphosa. It blamed failing municipal services, with water and power cuts and rising insecurity.

pieces.h: South Africa: the post-ANC era has already begun in the big cities

pieces.s: Nigrizia argued that the ANC is no longer the largest party in almost all the big urban areas, home to about a third of South Africans, marking the end of an era in the cities. It warned that who runs them may be decided “in the corridors of power” rather than at the ballot box, because coalition deals are struck behind closed doors while a law requiring more transparency is stuck in Parliament. It also linked the vote to months of anti-migrant violence and mass deportations.

pieces.h: In South Africa’s local elections, the historic Congress party had its worst result ever

pieces.s: Il Post reported the final count: 30.76% for the ANC, its worst result ever, against 24.64% for the DA, down from 46% in 2021. The DA won Cape Town outright and did well in Pretoria and Johannesburg, where it is expected to form coalitions without the ANC. Ramaphosa said the vote must be respected; turnout was 52%.

It argued the pact could shut the DA out of cities where it came first without immediately changing the national coalition, and that the stakes are high because the two provinces produce 48% of GDP.
